nuevos.titulo_original: A Big NAD Supplement Trial Just Backfired
nuevos.descripcion:
A big trial of a popular NAD supplement, nicotinamide riboside (NR), backfired in people with Parkinson's disease. NAD is a molecule central to our metabolism.

A team in Norway gave 410 people with early Parkinson's either 500 milligrams of NR twice a day or a placebo, for a year. On the standard Parkinson's rating scale, where a higher score is worse, the NR group scored 2.7 points worse than the placebo group.

A difference of 2.7 points sounds small, and it is. But NR was supposed to slow the disease down, and it went the wrong way.

The brain scans didn't show dopamine cells dying any faster, so this trial doesn't show that NR damaged people's brains. It shows that people felt and functioned worse on it.

This was a trial in people with Parkinson's, so it doesn't prove that NR harms healthy people. Even so, it undercuts the idea that, at worst, NR is harmless.
